task_intent: Map a mini research agenda on algorithmic fairness harms across the course lectures, with open questions and testable directions.
spine_must_hold: Agenda must distinguish at least two harm types (e.g. allocation vs quality-of-service vs representation), cite lecture grounding, and list research questions — not a pure advocacy op-ed.

gold_themes.description: Multiple harm kinds (allocation, QoS, representation) as fairness lecture frames them.
Mitigation can act at data/model/post-hoc stages (if lecture supports).
Connect fairness evaluation to ML systems lifecycle / monitoring debt.

gold_anti_themes.description: ImageNet/architecture race as the research core.

turns.user_template: Help me draft a mini research agenda on fairness harms grounded in our lectures.
Keep it to three research questions and one evaluation sketch; course-corpus only.
How should systems/lifecycle material change the agenda if at all?
What can this corpus not support, and what should I ask next?
Examiner fork: consider a short optional angle on privacy attacks vs fairness harms — only if useful — then return to the fairness agenda spine.

notes: Examiner-initiated fork (A6.5) — tests X-path without requiring system initiative.
